correctness.rationale: The published Knockoff+ threshold becomes \(P_k-rN_k\ge r\) at \(q=1/r\). Under the exact conditional sign-flip property this is a skip-free random walk with increments \(+1\) and \(-r\), each with probability one half, and selection is exactly first hitting level \(r\). The one-level defective generating function satisfies \(F(z)=z(1+F(z)^{r+1})/2\); strong Markov factorization gives \(F(z)^r\), and Lagrange inversion yields the submitted coefficients. A fresh exact-rational replay independently matched the closed sum to dynamic programming for multiple \(r\) and horizons and reproduced the displayed \(r=2\) and \(r=10\) limits.
correctness.risk: The exact formula requires reciprocal integer levels, tie-free nonzero magnitudes and the exact fair-sign property, exactly as stated.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact finite-sample and asymptotic calibration baseline for a widely used FDR procedure and quantifies how far the attained global-null error can sit below the nominal guarantee. The reciprocal-level staircase and explicit \(q=0.1\) limit are natural diagnostic quantities for theory and implementation.

final_claim: Under the complete null with distinct nonzero knockoff magnitudes and iid fair conditional signs, Knockoff+ at reciprocal level \(q=1/r\) has the stated finite Fuss-Catalan first-passage FDR formula and limiting value \(f_r^r\), where \(f_r\) is the smaller solution of \(2f=1+f^{r+1}\).
limitations: No statement is made for ties, approximate knockoffs, mixed null/non-null configurations, or non-reciprocal nominal levels.
Older target-decoy literature remains the main originality residual risk.
